final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate: the evidence supports aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a reversible 5% rollout with monitoring. But the enterprise policy is explicit that rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. The admissible evidence shows the opposite predicate remains unresolved: the medical device support segment is still included, the risk acceptance is incomplete and unapproved, and disclosure completion is not shown. That makes the caveat an unresolved compliance condition, not a minor qualification. For that reason, the record does not rise to compliant_with_caveats on the present evidence, even if a narrow operational-readiness narrative is supportable.
remaining_concerns: The affected medical device support segment remains exposed in the initial 5% rollout while below target on implant compatibility routing.
The policy condition for relying on rollout controls is not satisfied because the affected use case is neither excluded nor covered by reviewed and approved risk acceptance.
The record still does not show completed disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case before launch.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not mention the medical device support exposure.
Operational-readiness evidence supports a narrow launch-readiness argument, but it does not resolve the outstanding compliance predicate.
